questions.question: Which recurring whitespace or punctuation patterns correspond to language-defined word and boundary units?
Which recurring surface sequences are independently validated morphemes, and what distributional/function evidence supports each segmentation?
Which forms exhibit reproducible distributional behavior supporting lexical-category labels?
Do recurring forms show agreement relationships across independently annotated contexts?
Do the observed prefix and pairing candidates form a supported system, with what exceptions and agreement behavior?
Which candidate segments, alternations, and clause roles are supported by attested positive and negative examples?
Which recurring category combinations form evidence-supported phrases?
What constituent orders and argument relationships are present, and in which constructions?
Which complete constructions recur with independently adjudicated form and function?
How should the attested surface form a- be analyzed in its conflicting contexts?
Do stored records faithfully represent their source editions?

questions.evidence_note: No external linguistic sources or assumptions are imported; written character sequences alone do not establish sound values.
questions.question: What phonological or phonotactic generalizations, if any, follow from direct evidence?
Are the cited works independent by author as well as by source title?
Which corpus-wide contexts are positive, negative, exceptional, or competing evidence for each candidate?
